blocks.text: Podman runs rootless containers from the desktop account. The local client uses a shared Unix API for containers, images, networks and volumes; Docker-compatible commands and Compose clients can use the same engine. Help only documents commands and never contacts the engine.

The image reference selects a registry, namespace and tag. --rm removes the stopped container, --name gives it a stable name, and -it connects an interactive terminal. Review an image source and digest before using it with private data.

podman build --tag example-web:dev .
podman run --detach --name example-web --publish 8080:8080 example-web:dev
podman ps --all
podman logs --follow example-web
podman stop example-web
Run the build from the intended project directory. A Containerfile or build hook can execute code, so inspect it before building. Review published ports and stop containers you no longer need.

podman volume create example-data
podman run --rm --mount type=volume,source=example-data,destination=/var/lib/example docker.io/library/alpine:3.20
podman compose up --detach
podman compose down

Volumes outlive individual containers. Compose reads the compose file in the current directory and may create networks, containers and volumes. Check the file and the project secrets before starting it.
The shared socket grants control over the local engine. Prune, volume removal, image removal and reset operations can destroy data. Do not paste registry credentials into commands or logs.
